messages:
carla: Heads-up — ran into a nasty edge case with dequant fusion + KV cache during a canary. When rolling an INT8-attn variant over FP8, some shards had mixed KV encodings and we saw gibberish completions for ~30s. :grimacing:

dinesh: Ugh. Do you mean we kept the same KV layout but changed the quant path, or the shape/layout changed too?

carla: Same layout/shape. The runtime switched kernels mid-flight, and the fused dequant step assumed a homogeneous upstream dtype. In practice some requests hit fusion path A (INT8->FP32) and some hit fallback B (FP8->FP32) and we didn't have a handshake to flush/convert cached KV entries.

ben: Can you paste the minimal log snippet? Might help decide whether to force eviction or insert a conversion shim.

carla: Sure — snippet from canary node 3: 

```
[2026-10-03T14:12:01Z] kernel_select: picked quant_attn_int8_fused
[2026-10-03T14:12:01Z] kv_cache: served from shard-3 (dtype=int8)
[2026-10-03T14:12:05Z] kernel_select: picked quant_attn_fp8_mixed
[2026-10-03T14:12:05Z] kv_cache: served from shard-3 (dtype=fp8)
[2026-10-03T14:12:05Z] decode: dequant fusion mismatch -> falling back to generic dequant
[2026-10-03T14:12:06Z] request: partial tokens corrupted
```

carla: We didn't evict KV on kernel change and fusion assumed cache dtype stable.

emma: Do you think this was because of async routing? i.e., requests spawned on old kernel but then got routed to a new variant mid-request?

carla: Exactly. The routing policy allowed per-request fallback to cheaper variants when load spiked. That breakpoint is useful for cost but unsafe without atomic cache semantics.

ben: We have a few possible approaches: 1) conservative: force KV eviction on kernel dtype change (simple, available now, perf hit), 2) conversion shim: on first access convert cached KV from old dtype to new (cost amortized, tricky across shards), 3) attach dtype tag and disallow fusion if mixed clusters detected (safe but loses fusion perf). Thoughts?

dinesh: Option 2 is attractive if we can make conversion idempotent and async. But shard boundary coordination is the hard part. We need a lightweight protocol: 

```
on kernel_swap:
  mark shard KV with epoch++
  allow reads while conversion in background
  readers check epoch and await conversion threshold
```

emma: Background conversion risks latency spikes. Maybe hybrid: mark + lazy-convert first-N entries synchronously then background rest. Also use request-level hint: if request is latency-sensitive prefer eviction/pin to old kernel.

carla: Agreed. Also we discovered an additional problem: attention state quant noise. Converting FP8->INT8 then back is lossy in a way that changes top-k tokens for short sequences. So conversion fidelity matters per workload. We should surface per-deployed model a "safe quant transitions" flag based on evals.

ai-eval-bot: FYI — ran quick eval on example prompt set, INT8->FP8 roundtrip changed top-3 tokens in 12% of short-seq (<16) prompts, and 2% in long-seq (>128). Attaching eval_id: eval-20261003-09.

ben: Nice — that supports policy: for latency-critical endpoints mark rollout_policy: no-quant-transition or require conversion-safety >= 95%.

carla: From infra side, I think we should implement a 3-step rollout guard: 
1) on kernel variant activation, set shard.lifecycle = transitioning with dtype_old dtype_new metadata
2) any incoming request checks metadata and either: pin to old kernel, trigger sync-conversion for its keys, or route to a safe fallback model variant
3) once all hot keys converted or TTL expired, clear transitioning flag

sre: For observability, add metrics: kv_dtype_mismatch_count, conversion_latency_p50/p95, fusion_degraded_count. Alerts if mismatch_count > 0 for >10s.

dinesh: Implementation note: keep conversion code in runtime layer not in kernel to avoid per-kernel code explosion. Expose a small conversion API: convert_kv(shard_id, start_idx, end_idx, from_dtype, to_dtype) and make it resumable.

emma: Also we need unit tests + fuzzing for interleaved routing: simulate concurrent requests hitting convert + read + write to ensure no read-after-free of buffer.

carla: Good call. I'll open an RFC PR outlining the guard state machine and API. Quick poll: prefer eviction-by-default or convert-by-default?

ben: convert-by-default if conversion fidelity passes nightly evals and we have a safe resumable conversion. Otherwise eviction-by-default for canaries. :thumbsup:

dinesh: I'll prototype resumable conversion in a branch and wire basic metrics. If we hit fidelity or perf problems revert to eviction.

carla: Thanks — filing the RFC now and will tag the rollout checklist. For the immediate incident, I rolled back the canary and flushed KV on affected nodes.

infra-bot: deploy: canary rollback completed on cluster-22 by carla at 2026-10-03T14:20:12Z :white_check_mark:

carla: Closing loop — follow-up RFC: rfc/2026-10-03-quant-kv-transition.md (will link).
